bug_semantics: The IdentityServer profile page at /identity-server/account/profile is a cookie-authenticated UI that immediately commits email (and username) changes through DefaultUserService.UpdateAsync -> UserManager.SetEmailAsync with no confirmation step. The first-party PoC is not a token-less cross-site POST: an attacker uploads HTML as a Squidex asset and serves it inline on the same origin, then iframes the real profile form under a decoy overlay so the victim's click submits that form. Assets are delivered with Content-Disposition inline (unless download=1) and only Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none', which blocks stored XSS but not iframe/CSS UI-redress. Profile POSTs carry [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] and @Html.AntiForgeryToken() (the 7.4.0 CSRF fix), and antiforgery emits X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN unless identity.suppressXFrameOptionsHeader is true; SAMEORIGIN does not stop a same-origin asset iframe, so the antiforgery cookie/token travel with the clickjacked submit. Durable impact is changing the victim's email without verification and pivoting account recovery. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (CNA MITRE, CISA-ADP CWE-352); GHSA withdrawn_at is null.
flaw_origin: The profile email-change UI was first written in beb2a508bddfead9d9cbd495c1f24ce08d78ed1d (2017-05-28, 'Profile page.') as src/Squidex/Controllers/UI/Profile/ProfileController.cs POST /account/profile calling user.UpdateEmail(model.Email) with no antiforgery attribute, no frame-ancestors/'DENY' header, and no email re-verification, plus Views/Profile/Profile.cshtml posting Email without @Html.AntiForgeryToken(). Parent 11d08acc906de349e5b812f7ffdeaa232f226037 has no account/profile route and no ProfileController (only Angular profile-menu chrome). Later IdentityServer-area moves/refactors (route prefix /identity-server via IdentityServerController) reused that mechanism; they are not the BIC. 2da3c41da82eb945832f22bb70dba567ac6ce969 (in 7.4.0) only added antiforgery tokens/SAMEORIGIN, leaving same-origin clickjacking plus unverified SetEmailAsync intact through 7.21.0 and HEAD.

Framing: identity.suppressXFrameOptionsHeader defaults false and is copied onto AntiforgeryOptions.SuppressXFrameOptionsHeader (IdentityServerServices.cs), i.e. X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN on token-bearing profile responses, not DENY/frame-ancestors 'none'. No IdentityServer view sets CSP frame-ancestors.

Same-origin gadget: AssetContentController sets FileCallbackResult.SendInline = request.Download != 1; FileCallbackResultExecutor at 7.21.0/HEAD sets CSP script-src 'none' and Content-Disposition inline. HTML assets therefore render and may iframe same-origin identity UI.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-31016/GHSA-8hjx-7pv7-rr27 is an unreviewed MITRE CVE that labels CWE-352 CSRF, but the only first-party reproduction is same-origin clickjacking of /identity-server/account/profile hosted as an uploaded HTML asset, plus unverified email change. CVE.org is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected), so this is a real issue rather than FALSE_POSITIVE. Classic CSRF on this page was already closed in 7.4.0 by antiforgery (CVE-2023-0642); residual risk at 7.21.0 is UI-redress because SAMEORIGIN X-Frame-Options allows a same-origin iframe of the genuine token-bearing form, and SetEmailAsync still applies immediately. BIC search used git log --follow/--diff-filter=A on ProfileController.cs, then parent-tree verification: beb2a508bddfead9d9cbd495c1f24ce08d78ed1d is the smallest first write of the profile POST that changes email without framing protection or verification; parent 11d08acc906de349e5b812f7ffdeaa232f226037 lacks those files/routes. IdentityServer prefix and later refactors are moves, not a new origin. Tag membership: BIC is an ancestor of 7.21.0 and of HEAD; no later commit adds frame-ancestors 'none' or email confirmation, so there is no fix SHA. AI judgment used only the BIC commit object (2017 human author, no AI trailers); PR bodies and later 'AI improvements' commits were not used to attribute the introducer. Verdict NOT_AI, unpatched.
remaining_gap: Unpatched through HEAD bdff5054bbd8dd86932267f86e0543ed8d081810: no Squidex commit after 7.21.0 adds CSP frame-ancestors 'none'/X-Frame-Options DENY on IdentityServer profile pages or requires email re-verification before SetEmailAsync.

unpatched.reason: No upstream fix commit exists. 7.22.0, 7.23.0, and HEAD bdff5054bbd8dd86932267f86e0543ed8d081810 still expose /identity-server/account/profile as a SAMEORIGIN-frameable antiforgery form that calls SetEmailAsync without confirmation; changelogs after 7.21.0 do not mention clickjacking, frame-ancestors, or profile email verification. CVE.org lists no patched versions.

potential_fix.approach: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' (and X-Frame-Options: DENY) on IdentityServer account/profile GET/POST responses, and require out-of-band confirmation of the new address before DefaultUserService.UpdateAsync commits SetEmailAsync/SetUserNameAsync.
potential_fix.rationale: frame-ancestors 'none' blocks the same-origin HTML-asset iframe that bypasses antiforgery X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN; confirming the new email stops a clickjacked Save from taking over account recovery even if framing is later re-enabled.
